utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-8/1-I, the Prosecutor versus Dusan Fustar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, may I have the appearances, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Camille Bibles and Mark Vlasic are here for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. We are Theodore Scudder and Dragan Ivetic for the defendant Dusan Fustar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fustar, would you please stand up? I'd like to make sure that you are hearing the proceedings in a language that you speak and understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear these proceedings in a language that I do understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: May I have your full name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 29th of June 1954, Dusan Fustar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My name is Kwon and I'm a judge of Trial Chamber 3 to which this case was already assigned. This is the initial appearance to be conducted in accordance with Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. According to the Rules the first thing to deal with at this time is to check the -- whether the right of the accused to counsel is protected. However, as I note, Mr. Fustar is already being represented by counsel. I don't think I need to mention it at this moment. The next thing to be done is the reading out of the indictment. It is the right of the accused to have the indictment read out in full in a language he speaks and understands. And it is also the duty of the Court to satisfy itself that the accused understands the indictment. However, a kind of practice has developed in this Tribunal whereby an accused can waive his right to have the indictment to be read out, especially in a case where he is represented by counsel. Mr. Scudder and Mr.Ivetic may I know if you have discussed this matter with your client and whether Mr. Fustar wishes to have his indictment read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have discussed it with Mr. Fustar. He's informed us that he has read the indictment in his own language and after discussing it with us, he would waive a formal reading of all of the wording of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. May I take your words as meaning your that client understands the contends of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then the next step will be the entry of a plea to the charges of the indictment. The accused may enter a plea within 30 days of the initial appearance but he may enter a plea today, the day of initial appearance, if he so wishes. Mr. Scudder what is your client's intention? Does he wish to enter a plea today or do it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Mr. Fustar is prepared to enter his plea today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, then if he wishes to enter a plea, yes, will you please stand up again? I know that to my understanding there are 42 counts in this indictment but among them, Mr. Fustar is charged with seven counts, that is namely counts 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11. So Madam Registrar, could you put the counts, each count, to the accused, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia pursuant to her authority in Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, charges Dusan Fustar with: Count 3: Persecutions on political, racial or religious grounds, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 4: Inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 5: Outrages upon personal dignity, a violation of the laws and customs of war as recognised by Article 3(1)(c) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. In addition, Dusan Fustar is criminally responsible for the crimes set forth in counts 3 to 5 pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 8: Murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(A), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and. Count 9: Murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Or in the alternative, Count 10: Inhuman acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 11: Cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you understand the content of the charges, charges against you. And I'll put each count to you so please give me your plea. The first count 3 is persecution as a crime against humanity. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The count 4 is inhumane acts as a crime against humanity. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. The count 5 is outrages upon human dignity as violation of the laws or customs of war.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And count 8 is murder as crime against humanity. How do you plead to that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And count 9 is murder as violation of the laws or customs of war. How do you plead to that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And count 10 is inhumane acts as a crime against humanity. How do you plead to that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And count 11, finally, the cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war. How do you plead to that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, the accused pleads not guilty to all the charges. And now I turn to the Prosecution. As you may be well aware, it is the duty of the Prosecutor to make available all the supporting materials, together with the accused's statements, within 30 days - is it right? - to the Defence in a language the accused understands. Are there any problems in disclosing these materials?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. In fact, we've met with learned counsel about that issue and we have copies, both in English and B/C/S, ready to hand to them today. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, today?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Are there any issues to raise -- for the parties to raise at this moment? From the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have two additional issues. Both are primarily a matter of courtesy to the Court. First, as we have indicated in the Banovic case, three of the original accused in this case have been resolved and therefore we are amending the indictment to make it a more precise document for trial in this matter. We are additionally amending the indictment to bring it into conformity with some of the recent court rulings, and that would apply obviously with this accused as well. Second, Your Honour, we are -- have been advised or were aware that members of learned counsel's law firm have represented other individuals in this matter, and we have again discussed this with them, and we would just like to put on record or have them discuss with the Court the fact that their client is aware of that issue and is willing to proceed with them as counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then you have -- certainly you have your say. Yes, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Your Honour, both Mr. Ivetic and I are members of a firm in Chicago, United States, with a Mr. Jovan Ostojic, who represented another man in this case, his name was Kolundzija. We have discussed with Mr. Fustar that we both practise law with Mr. Ostojic, who represented Mr. Kolundzija, and he is aware of that and he wishes to proceed with us as his counsel. He does not see any problem with that. I believe he's fully aware of the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have any opinion about the amendment of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: No. The Prosecutors explained that to us before we came here today, and we understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. I have one thing to inform you, that according to the rule 65 ter, a Pre-Trial Judge may be assisted in the performance of his duties by one of the Senior Legal Officers assigned to chambers. And in this regard, I would like Mrs. Yvonne Featherstone, a SLO assigned to Trial Chamber III, to meet with the parties on a regular basis to discuss matters for the preparation of the trial and the -- such as the establishment of work plan or something like that. And my understanding is that Ms. Featherstone has already made an appointment with the Prosecution and Defence for the Banovic brothers on, if my memory is correct, 18th of February, not far from now. So I would like to request, especially Defence counsel, to take time and to meet her, and to join the meeting, to discuss everything about this procedure. If anything -- there is nothing to raise for the parties -- Oh, Mr. Fustar, is there anything you'd like to raise at this moment regarding the proceedings or anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then this case is adjourned. Well, I'm sorry, the next Status Conference is fixed on -- for Banovic brothers, on Friday, 10th of May, 2002, this year, and certainly this case will be linked up with that case. The case is adjourned.
